question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT formula for electric power?
solution:
The correct answer is **__P=V/I__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **The electric power is given by **P = VI**, where V is the potential difference, **I** is the **electric current** and** P** is the** electric power**. 
 
• The unit of electrical power is the **watt**. 
 
• 1 W is the power consumed by a device that carries 1 A of current when operated at a potential difference of 1 V.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​​It is **the rate at which work is done or energy is transformed in an electrical circuit**. Simply put, it is a measure of how much energy is used in a span of time. In physics, the rate of transfer of electrical energy by an electrical circuit per unit of time is called an electrical power.
 
• **Electrical power is the product of voltage times current.**
